blockers.finding: Clause PROB/stationary (eps-stationary point: E||grad f(xbar)||^2 <= eps) is owned by unit alg, whose PROB mapping is [Query, Reply, eventOracle, arrivalOracle]. None of these declarations expresses eps-stationarity; the notion appears only in the successful predicates of RingmasterIterations.spec and RingmasterUniversalTime.spec. The node:PROB check at statement review would therefore find the owned clause unrealized in its mapped declarations.
blockers.repair: Either (a) add to unit alg a Prop-valued definition of eps-stationarity (e.g. integrability of ||gradient f (x w)||^2 and its integral <= eps under a probability measure), map PROB to it, and use it in both successful predicates; or (b) move ownership of PROB/stationary (or PROB) to setup_iter, map it to outputs.Setups.RingmasterIterations.spec, and have setup_time reuse the same predicate. Keep PROB/problem mapped to Query/Reply/oracles.

IID (measurable coordinates, iIndepFun, marginal mu) for the stream P; the k-th oracle call uses the k-th coordinate (Oracle.answer k ... (seed k)), which is the accepted i.i.d.-stream reading of L151.

iters records the iteration of each worker's point; delays k = iters of the arriving worker; delays_bound proves a_k <= k < a_k + R (L1371).

step restarts every worker j with R <= (k+1) - iters j at x^{k+1} and time t right after update k (i.e. at the top of the next loop at the same instant); this is exactly the stop rule of L502 with delay = current iteration - assigned iteration.
step on reply (i,t,G): x^{k+1} = x^k - gamma G, worker i restarts at x^{k+1}, count + 1; matches L504-507. Ties processed sequentially (earliest picks lowest index).

T41 -> public_iter: result : Convergence outputs.Setups.RingmasterIterations.spec budget; spec encodes T41's complete context; algorithm pinned to ringmaster.
Headline: K iterate updates (natural number), satisfying the horizon; recorded separately from oracle calls.

Execution: one oracle (index 0) with budget p.K; each call returns one arrival (one update); the algorithm queries none after K updates. All K calls are used for updates since arrivalOracle always answers.
Conversion: K calls = K updates, witnessed by advance_ringmaster (planned in exec, within public_iter's dependency closure).
T51 -> public_time with spec outputs.Setups.RingmasterUniversalTime.spec; algorithm pinned; successful preserves both the accuracy and the T_Kbar time headline.
Headline: time T_Kbar in seconds, domain [0, +infinity] (ENNReal), distinct from oracle calls; preserved in successful as ofReal(clock) <= deadline.

Execution: one oracle with budget max 1 ceil(sigma^2/eps) * ceil(48 L Delta/eps) = R*Kbar calls = publicInput K; under deadline < top every call yields an arrival (deadline_updates); a none reply leaves the state unchanged.

Conversion witnesses deadline_updates (first R*Kbar arrivals exist, clock <= T_Kbar) and advance_ringmaster (execution = recursion), both planned in exec within public_time's closure. The relationship between seconds and calls is via the proved clock bound, not by identification.
setup_iter is used only by T41; shared hypotheses/parameters equal T41's result_context exactly; spec fields (valid, admissible, successful) encode them. Identical mode justified.

setup_time is used only by T51; shared lists equal T51's result_context; it reuses stepSize from setup_iter (a definition, not hypotheses). Identical mode justified; the two setups are not merged, so no context is strengthened.

notes: Feasibility only (not evidence): the draft dev/outputs modules elaborate the planned interfaces; the algorithm's step, the oracles, and the setups' valid/admissible/successful fields match the plan text.
T41's arrivalOracle reports time 0 for every arrival, so T41's output clock is meaningless; harmless because T41 claims no time bound.
n = 0 makes T41's admissible predicate unsatisfiable (no arrive : N -> Fin 0), so T41 is vacuous there; the source assumes workers exist.
Delta and K (T41) / K = R*Kbar (T51) are public inputs; this is the accepted packaging of the source's averaged/selected-iterate guarantee and follows existing repository setups (RennalaUniformTime).

Declarations stepSize/publicInput (setup_iter) and threshold (setup_time) are not mapped to clause-owning nodes for T41/T51 clauses; they are reached through the spec in the result types, which is acceptable but should be inspected under node:T41/node:T51.
